about: The AP Biology app pages. scripts/build-apbio.mjs writes each page's shell (head, header, footer, a <div id="app"> mount) from this file; the page's behavior is its script in bio/assets/<script>, which mounts into #app. Until that script exists the shell says the page arrives with the first published unit. "static": true marks a generated page that is not an app (teachers.html). premium names the Premium feature (ApBioCore gates it); card is the line on the course home. No path may contain the token "ap" (docs/apbio-spec.md decision 2), so scripts live in bio/assets/pages/, not apps/. tools[] are the simulators, skills tools and drills: page bio/tools/<slug>.html, script bio/assets/tools/<slug>.js, content bio/data/tools/<slug>.json (docs/apbio-architecture.md, Tools).

apps.title: Practice questions
apps.desc: Biology practice by unit, topic or science practice: standalone questions and data-heavy stimulus sets, with an explanation for every option.
apps.card: Drill a unit, a topic or a science practice, with stimulus sets.

apps.title: Spaced review
apps.desc: Your biology spaced review queue: every question you missed comes back just before you would forget it.
apps.card: Missed questions come back when you are about to forget them.

apps.title: Unit tests and practice exams
apps.desc: Timed biology unit tests and full practice exams in the hybrid format: 60 multiple-choice questions, then six free-response questions with rubrics.
apps.card: Unit tests and full timed practice exams, scored with rubrics.

apps.title: Free-response practice
apps.desc: Biology free-response practice in all six question types, each with a point-by-point rubric, a full-credit sample answer and a printable answer sheet.
apps.card: All six free-response types, with rubrics and sample answers.

apps.title: Flashcards
apps.desc: Spaced-repetition biology flashcards built from the glossary, by unit and topic.

apps.title: Simulators and skills tools
apps.desc: Biology simulators and skills tools: enzymes, osmosis, the cell cycle, Hardy-Weinberg, chi-square, graph building and more, each followed by questions.
apps.card: Simulators, then the questions about what you saw.

apps.title: Your dashboard
apps.desc: Your biology mastery by unit, topic and science practice, with every miss linked to the lesson that teaches it.
apps.card: Mastery by unit, topic and science practice.

apps.title: Search the course
apps.desc: Search every biology lesson, notes page, glossary term and tool in the course.

apps.title: For teachers
apps.desc: For biology teachers: stable share links, printable notes and unit sheets, and sharing pages to Google Classroom, with no new student data collected.
apps.lede: Share any notes page, lesson or unit sheet with a stable link. Students need no account, and nothing they do leaves their device unless they choose to sign in.

tools.name: Osmosis and water potential
tools.title: Osmosis and water potential simulator
tools.desc: Put a potato core, a red blood cell or a dialysis bag into a solution and watch water potential decide which way water moves, then answer questions about it.
tools.blurb: Compare water potential inside and out, watch the mass change, and build the potato core graph.

tools.name: Enzyme activity and inhibition
tools.title: Enzyme activity and inhibition simulator
tools.desc: Change substrate, temperature, pH and inhibitors, run trials and watch the reaction rate, then answer questions about enzyme kinetics and inhibition.
tools.blurb: Saturation, temperature and pH optima, and competitive against noncompetitive inhibitors, with data you collect.

tools.name: Signal transduction and amplification
tools.title: Signal transduction and amplification simulator
tools.desc: Follow epinephrine through a G protein, cAMP and a kinase cascade, count molecules at each step, block steps with drugs and toxins, and watch the signal end.
tools.blurb: Receptor to response: where a signal is amplified, how it is switched off, and what each block does.

tools.name: Cell cycle checkpoints
tools.title: Cell cycle checkpoints simulator
tools.desc: Grow cells with growth factor, DNA damage, cancer mutations or a spindle poison, and watch the phases, DNA content and which damaged cells divide.
tools.blurb: G1, G2 and M checkpoints, p53, Rb and oncogenes, with a DNA content histogram.

tools.name: Meiosis and nondisjunction
tools.title: Meiosis and nondisjunction simulator
tools.desc: Step one cell through meiosis I and II, switch crossing over on, choose how each pair lines up, make a pair fail to separate and count the chromosomes in every gamete and zygote.
tools.blurb: Crossing over, independent assortment and 2ⁿ, n+1 and n−1 gametes, and a comparison with mitosis.

tools.name: Lac and trp operons
tools.title: Lac and trp operons simulator
tools.desc: Set glucose, lactose or tryptophan, add mutations such as lacI⁻, a super-repressor or an Oᶜ operator, and watch the repressor, CAP, RNA polymerase, mRNA and enzyme respond over time.
tools.blurb: Inducible and repressible operons, CAP–cAMP, repressor mutations and the mRNA–enzyme lag.

tools.name: Mean, SD and standard error
tools.title: Mean, standard deviation and standard error practice
tools.desc: Practice the mean, median, range, sample standard deviation and standard error, with every step of the working shown after you check.
tools.blurb: Summarize a data set: mean, median, range, standard deviation and standard error.

tools.name: Confidence intervals and error bars
tools.title: Confidence intervals and error bars practice
tools.desc: Practice 95% confidence intervals as mean plus or minus 2 SE, draw them as error bars, and decide what overlap tells you.
tools.blurb: Turn mean, SD and n into a 95% confidence interval and read overlapping error bars.

tools.name: Chi-square test
tools.title: Chi-square test practice
tools.desc: Practice the chi-square goodness-of-fit test: expected counts, the chi-square value, degrees of freedom, the critical value and the decision.
tools.blurb: Expected counts, χ², degrees of freedom, the critical value table and the decision.

tools.name: Rates and percent change
tools.title: Rates and percent change practice
tools.desc: Practice calculating rates of change from data tables and percent change between measurements, with the working shown step by step.
tools.blurb: Rates from data tables and percent change, with units and signs.

tools.name: Water potential calculations
tools.title: Water potential calculations practice
tools.desc: Practice solute potential and water potential calculations and predict which way water moves, with every step shown.
tools.blurb: Solute potential, water potential and the direction water moves.

tools.name: Hardy-Weinberg calculations
tools.title: Hardy-Weinberg calculations practice
tools.desc: Practice Hardy-Weinberg calculations: allele frequencies from genotype counts or a recessive trait, and expected genotype frequencies.
tools.blurb: Allele and genotype frequencies with p + q = 1 and p² + 2pq + q² = 1.

tools.name: Simpson’s diversity index
tools.title: Simpson’s diversity index practice
tools.desc: Practice Simpson’s diversity index from species counts, with every step of the calculation shown.
tools.blurb: How diverse is a community? D = 1 − Σ(n/N)² from species counts.

tools.name: Graph builder
tools.title: Graph construction practice
tools.desc: Build a graph from a data table: choose the type, set the axes, labels and scale, plot the points and error bars, and get feedback on each part.
tools.blurb: Graph type, axes, labels with units, scale, points and error bars, each checked.

tools.name: Experimental design and argumentation
tools.title: Experimental design and argumentation drills
tools.desc: Drills on independent and dependent variables, controls and what they rule out, null hypotheses, claim-evidence-reasoning, and prediction with mechanism.
tools.blurb: Variables, controls and their justification, null hypotheses, claim-evidence-reasoning, prediction and mechanism.
